title: Telemetry hygiene: tenant-scoped retention, adaptive redaction heuristics, and trace RBAC
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement tenant-scoped retention windows and an adaptive PII redaction pipeline for traces, metrics labels, and logs. Add fine-grained RBAC for trace visibility and immutable access-audit events. Deliverables: (1) retention policy engine for per-tenant TTLs on spans/logs/metrics, (2) streaming redaction heuristics with configgable rulesets and sampling-awareness, (3) trace-level RBAC and access-audit hooks, (4) migration and backfill plan for existing telemetry backends.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant retention TTLs can be configured in the Console and enforced in the ingestion pipeline (min 1d, max 7y) and verified via retention-check job
Streaming redaction removes or tokenizes IPs, keys, and 3rd-party PII across spans/attributes/logs in >99% of our test prompt corpus without breaking structured trace search
Sampling-aware redaction preserves KV-cache-sensitive prefixes so production latency impact is <5% at p95 under typical load
RBAC enforces trace visibility at the tenant and team level and emits immutable access-audit events to the audit stream with tenant-id and actor
Migration plan includes zero-downtime rollout and a rollback path; automated tests simulate tenant-specific TTLS and redaction rules
Performance regression on ingestion pipeline is measured and no-more-than 10% increase in cost per ingested event is observed on staging
tasks: Design retention engine schema and API (Console + API surface)
Prototype streaming redaction service and integrate with tracing agent
Add RBAC checks to trace-query path and attach access-audit hook
Implement tenant-ttl enforcement in storage compactor and S3 lifecycle hooks
Create e2e tests and load tests for latency and correctness
Write migration plan and runbook for existing telemetry buckets
Ship docs and Console UX for rule management

2025-02-25 - Eng review (Liam Chen): Opted to make redaction rules pluginable (regex + deterministic tokenizers) to avoid multiple release cycles.
2025-03-01 - Security (I. Novak): Asked for HSM-backed key rotation notes and a threat-model appendix prior to security sign-off.
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting completed; scoped MVP to spans+logs first, metrics labels second.
2025-02-17: Prototype streaming redaction (Go) can process 10k events/s per core using combinable tokenizers; initial perf looks promising.
2025-02-22: Retention engine schema landed (PR 3388) - storage compactor changes require migration job.
2025-02-28: RBAC model v1 implemented in query path; integration tests added to ensure audits are emitted.
2025-03-04: Load test on staging (10k eps) shows 7% ingestion CPU increase when redaction enabled with default rules; next: optimize rule compilation and hot-path memcopies.
decision_log: Rule engine approach: chose deterministic tokenization + regex matchers vs full NLP scrubbing to keep latency predictable and to allow deterministic tests.
Sampling strategy: apply redaction at ingestion stage but allow bypass for sampled raw traces stored in a tenant-isolated cold bucket for advanced debugging (opt-in, audited).
Retention defaults: set default to 90 days for standard, 365 days for enterprise, with explicit min and max guardrails in Console.
RBAC granularity: decided to scope at trace and span metadata level rather than per-field to reduce complexity for query planning and caching.
